title: A day on Venus outlasts its year
hook: Venus turns so slowly that it orbits the Sun before it spins once.
peek: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once but only about 225 to orbit the Sun. It also spins backwards, so on Venus the Sun rises in the west, very slowly.
lede: Venus takes about 225 Earth days to go around the Sun and about 243 Earth days to turn once on its axis. So one rotation lasts longer than its year. It also spins in the opposite direction to most planets, so the Sun rises in the west. Because its thick clouds hide the surface, astronomers only measured this with radar in the 1960s.

bullets.text: Sunrise to sunrise is a different measure. Because Venus spins backwards while it orbits, the two motions combine, and a Venusian solar day lasts about 117 Earth days.
The surface turns slowly, but the upper atmosphere races around the planet in about four Earth days, far faster than the ground beneath it.

In 2012 the European Venus Express probe found the planet turning about six and a half minutes slower than NASA's Magellan had measured in the early 1990s. Drag from the heavy atmosphere may be part of the reason.
Nobody knows for sure. Ideas include a giant collision early in its history and the slow drag of its heavy atmosphere and the Sun's tides. Both remain hypotheses.
